public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Integrality and supercongruences of the factorial ratio $\frac{(6n)! n!}{(3n)! (2n)!^2}$

Integral factorial ratio sequence:
$$a(n) = \frac{(30n)! n!}{(15n)! (10n)! (6n)!}$$

*References:*
- [A211417](https://oeis.org/A211417)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA211417


/--
Integral factorial ratio sequence:
$$a(n) = \frac{(30n)! n!}{(15n)! (10n)! (6n)!}$$
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (Nat.factorial (30 * n) * Nat.factorial n) /
  (Nat.factorial (15 * n) * Nat.factorial (10 * n) * Nat.factorial (6 * n))

open Nat Int Finset

def coprimeIndices (r : ℕ) : Finset ℕ :=
  (Finset.range (r + 1)).filter (fun i => 1 ≤ i ∧ Nat.gcd i 30 = 1)

/--
The product term in the denominator of the general conjecture:
$$\prod_{i = 1..r, i \text{ coprime to } 30} (30n - i)$$
We define this in ℤ to handle the $n=0$ case where $30n-i$ in the product might be negative.
-/
def divisorProduct (n r : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  (coprimeIndices r).prod (fun i : ℕ => 30 * (n : ℤ) - (i : ℤ))


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 77636318760 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 53837289804317953893960 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 43880754270176401422739454033276880 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 38113558705192522309151157825210540422513019720 := by rfl


/--
It appears that $a(n)/(30n - 1)$ is integral for all $n$ (checked up to $n = 1000$). - _Peter Bala_, Aug 28 2025

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/211417.wip.lean#L243"]
theorem thirty_mul_sub_one_dvd_a (n : ℕ) : (30 * (n : ℤ) - 1) ∣ (a n : ℤ) := by
    sorry

/--
Conjecture: "7*a(n)/(2*n + 1) ... [is an] integer for all n (checked up to n = 1000)."
- _Peter Bala_, Aug 28 2025
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,

    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/oeis-a211417/blob/cad1fb228b5b80573cab3eeb92c8be57fd73c506/lean/OeisA211417FC.lean#L866-L868"]
theorem seven_mul_a_dvd_two_mul_add_one (n : ℕ) :
    (2 * (n : ℤ) + 1) ∣ 7 * (a n : ℤ) := by
  sorry

/--
Conjecture: "a(n)/(3*n + 1) ... [is an] integer for all n (checked up to n = 1000)."
- _Peter Bala_, Aug 28 2025
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/oeis-a211417/blob/cad1fb228b5b80573cab3eeb92c8be57fd73c506/lean/OeisA211417FC.lean#L1173-L1175"]
theorem a_dvd_three_mul_add_one (n : ℕ) :
    (3 * (n : ℤ) + 1) ∣ (a n : ℤ) := by
  sorry

/--
Conjecture: "a(n)/(5*n + 1) ... [is an] integer for all n (checked up to n = 1000)."
- _Peter Bala_, Aug 28 2025
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/oeis-a211417/blob/cad1fb228b5b80573cab3eeb92c8be57fd73c506/lean/OeisA211417FC.lean#L1446-L1448"]
theorem a_dvd_five_mul_add_one (n : ℕ) :
    (5 * (n : ℤ) + 1) ∣ (a n : ℤ) := by
  sorry

/--
Conjecture: "42*a(n)/((2*n + 1)*(3*n + 1)*(5*n + 1)) [is an] integer for all n
(checked up to n = 1000)." - _Peter Bala_, Aug 28 2025
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/oeis-a211417/blob/cad1fb228b5b80573cab3eeb92c8be57fd73c506/lean/OeisA211417FC.lean#L1514-L1524"]
theorem forty_two_mul_a_dvd_product (n : ℕ) :
    ((2 * (n : ℤ) + 1) * (3 * (n : ℤ) + 1) * (5 * (n : ℤ) + 1)) ∣
      42 * (a n : ℤ) := by
  sorry

/--
Conjecture: "More generally, for r >= 1, we conjecture that there exists a constant D(r) such that
D(r)*a(n)/Product_{i = 1..r, i coprime to 30} (30*n - i) is integral for all n."
- _Peter Bala_, Aug 28 2025

This generalizes `thirty_mul_sub_one_dvd_a` (the $r = 1$ case where $D(1) = 1$).

**Proof sketch** (kernel-checked development at the `formal_proof` permalink below, which
proves the non-vacuous form with the explicit positive witness $D = (r!)^{r^2}$):
Legendre-valuation analysis of the Landau step function
$\Delta(x) = \lfloor 30x \rfloor + \lfloor x \rfloor - \lfloor 15x \rfloor -
\lfloor 10x \rfloor - \lfloor 6x \rfloor$, whose values lie in $\{0, 1\}$. Three
ingredients: a unit-class rigidity lemma ($\Delta_c = 1$ for every unit class $c$ modulo
$30$), a witness-uniqueness bound for prime powers $p^k > r$ (at most one factor of the
divisor product is divisible by $p^k$), and a uniform low-layer budget for $p^k \le r$
absorbed by the witness constant.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/chy4pro/formal-conjectures/blob/fbc6706451b0e80787580d91ee6c252c121e0165/FormalConjectures/OEIS/211417.lean#L555"]
theorem general_divisibility (r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) :
    ∃ D : ℤ, 0 < D ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, (divisorProduct n r) ∣ (D * (a n : ℤ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Supercongruence: "a(p^k) == a(p^(k-1)) ( mod p^(3*k) ) for any prime p >= 5 and any positive
integer k." - _Peter Bala_, Jan 24 2020

More generally, "the congruences a(n*p^k) == a(n*p^(k-1)) ( mod p^(3*k) ) may hold for any
prime p >= 5 and any positive integers n and k."
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem supercongruence (p k : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hp5 : 5 ≤ p) (hk : 0 < k) :
    (p : ℤ) ^ (3 * k) ∣ ((a (p ^ k) : ℤ) - (a (p ^ (k - 1)) : ℤ)) := by
  sorry

end OeisA211417

findings.description: The module docstring's title reads "Integrality and supercongruences of the factorial ratio $\frac{(6n)! n!}{(3n)! (2n)!^2}$". That is a different sequence: at n = 1 it equals 720/(6·4) = 30, while A211417(1) = 77636318760. Everything else in the file is about (30n)! n!/((15n)! (10n)! (6n)!): the next line of the module docstring, `def a`, the test lemmas and every theorem. The title looks copied from a neighbouring factorial-ratio sequence. No Lean statement is affected.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A211417 %N: "a(n) = (30*n)!*n!/((15*n)!*(10*n)!*(6*n)!)." (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A211/A211417.seq, rev #94). The title's ratio is exactly OEIS A061162 %N: "a(n) = (6n)!n!/((3n)!(2n)!^2)." A211417's %Y line cross-references A061162.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the title to `# Integrality and supercongruences of the factorial ratio $\frac{(30n)!\, n!}{(15n)!\,(10n)!\,(6n)!}$`.

status_issues.source_status: Solved classically, and the source says so. Since Peter Bala's comment of Jan 24 2020 (unchanged in the 2024 snapshot and in the current rev #94), OEIS A211417 states the n = 1 congruence as a proved fact, with a proof pointer. Only the generalization to a(n·p^k) is left conjectural ("may hold").
status_issues.evidence:
OEIS A211417: "Congruences: a(p^k) == a(p^(k-1)) ( mod p^(3*k) ) for any prime p >= 5 and any positive integer k (write a(n) as C(30*n,15*n)*C(15*n,5*n)/C(6*n,n) and use equation 39 in Mestrovic, p. 12). More generally, the congruences a(n*p^k) == a(n*p^(k-1)) ( mod p^(3*k) ) may hold ..." The file's docstring drops the parenthetical proof pointer.

Mestrovic (arXiv:1111.3057), 39th numbered equation (LaTeX label con36): for any prime p ≥ 5, C(np^a, mp^a) ≡ C(np^{a-1}, mp^{a-1}) (mod p^{3a}). This is a corollary of the Jacobsthal–Kazandzidis congruence.

Derivation (my check):
- Apply it to C(30p^k,15p^k), C(15p^k,5p^k) and C(6p^k,p^k).
- C(6p^{k-1},p^{k-1}) is prime to p: by Kummer, adding p^{k-1} and 5p^{k-1} in base p gives no carry for p ≥ 5.
- Hence a(p^k) = C(30p^k,15p^k)·C(15p^k,5p^k)/C(6p^k,p^k) ≡ a(p^{k-1}) (mod p^{3k}), which is exactly the Lean statement.

Numerics (Lean #eval): v_p(a(p^k) − a(p^{k-1})) ≥ 3k in every case tested (p=5,7 with k≤3; p=11,13,17 with k≤2; p=19,23,29,31 with k=1).

The KitaKen1 proof file linked from this file leaves the same target as `sorry`, noting "Planned route: Jacobsthal--Kazandzidis for three binomial coefficients, then cancellation."
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the category to `@[category research solved, AMS 11]`. Restore Bala's proof pointer (Jacobsthal–Kazandzidis / Mestrovic eq. (39)) in the docstring. If the file should contain the genuinely open problem, add it as a separate `research open` variant: `theorem supercongruence.variants.general (n p k : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (hp : p.Prime) (hp5 : 5 ≤ p) (hk : 0 < k) : (p : ℤ) ^ (3 * k) ∣ (a (n * p ^ k) : ℤ) - a (n * p ^ (k - 1))`.

reformulations.difference: `a n` uses truncating ℕ division `(30n)! n! / ((15n)! (10n)! (6n)!)`, not the rational ratio.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The ratio is always an integer (Chebyshev/Landau; Peter Bala's proof, linked from A211417, shows floor(15x)+floor(10x)+floor(6x) ≤ floor(30x)+floor(x)). So the ℕ division is exact and `a n` equals A211417(n). Checked by #eval: the numerator is divisible by the denominator for n < 30, and the test lemmas agree with the b-file for n ≤ 4.

reformulations.difference: The source asks for "a constant D(r) > 0" such that D(r)·a(n)/∏(30n−i) is integral for all n. The Lean takes D : ℤ with 0 < D, n ranges over all of ℕ including 0, and the ratio is written as ℤ-divisibility.
reformulations.equivalence_argument:
1. Any positive real constant that works is a positive integer: at n = 0, D·a(0)/∏(−i) = ±D/∏i must be an integer, so D ∈ ℤ.
2. Conversely, an integer D is a constant.
3. Including n = 0 does not change solvability: if D works for n ≥ 1, then D·∏_{i∈S_r} i also works at n = 0.
4. The divisor ∏(30n − i) is never 0, because each i is coprime to 30.

could_not_verify: OeisA211417.general_divisibility: its formal_proof link points into a personal fork of formal-conjectures (chy4pro/formal-conjectures), which I deliberately did not open. I checked the statement's truth myself, so the `research solved` tag is justified mathematically. By Legendre's formula, v_p(a(n)) = Σ_k Δ(n/p^k), where Δ = ⌊30x⌋+⌊x⌋−⌊15x⌋−⌊10x⌋−⌊6x⌋. Δ = 1 on [c/30,(c+1)/30) for every unit c mod 30, and a prime power p^k > r divides at most one factor. So D = ∏_{p≤r} p^{r⌊log_p r⌋} works; numerically this holds for r ≤ 31, n ≤ 40. I did not check the linked formal artifact itself.
review.notes:
1. `supercongruence` states the n = 1 congruence faithfully, so the defect is only its `research open` tag (see status_issues). The truly open claim in Bala's comment, a(n·p^k) ≡ a(n·p^{k−1}) (mod p^{3k}) for all n ≥ 1, is quoted in the docstring but formalized nowhere in the file. It holds numerically for p ∈ {5,7,11,13}, k ∈ {1,2}, n ≤ 12. That includes every tested n where p divides C(6np^{k−1}, np^{k−1}), where the simple unit argument breaks down. Adding it as a `research open` variant would give the file an actual open problem.

2. Bala's other generalization in the same comment is also not formalized. For k ∈ {2,3,5}, it asks for a constant C(k,r) > 0 with C(k,r)·a(n)/∏_{i≤r, gcd(i,k)=1}(kn+i) integral. This is a missing variant, not a defect.

3. The `general_divisibility` docstring quotes the conjecture without the "> 0" that the current OEIS text has ("a constant D(r) > 0"). The Lean has `0 < D`, which matches the current source. I could not tell whether the original Aug 2025 wording had "> 0": GitHub rate-limited me, and the earliest post-2025 archive (Sep 2026) already has it.

4. The "solved" tags check out:
   - The four `formal_proof using lean4` claims (KitaKen1, commit cad1fb2) compile against this exact checkout with no errors. Their targets restate the file's theorems verbatim and depend only on [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].
   - For `thirty_mul_sub_one_dvd_a`, the AlphaProof Nexus file linked from OEIS proves the identical `(30 * (n : ℤ) - 1) ∣ (a n : ℤ)` with an identical `a`. OEIS and Adamczewski (arXiv:2608.11941) also record it as proved.
   - OEIS itself records only the (30n−1) conjecture as proved. The file's other solved tags rest on the formal proofs above, and on my own argument for `general_divisibility`.
